text: No principality is secure without having its own forces; on the contrary, it is entirely dependent on good fortune, not having the valour which in adversity would defend it. And it has always been the opinion and judgment of wise men that nothing can be so uncertain or unstable as fame or power not founded on its own strength.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter XIII, Concerning auxiliaries, mixed soldiery, and one's own
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
